HCP2 Forest Review
Project Ember · Epic 5 · Human checkpoint 2

The forest is real

● Awaiting your sign-off

Three Queens with every tree Terrain placed: 5,861,933 of them, Douglas-fir, ponderosa pine, grand fir, sagebrush and bunchgrass. You're judging whether density and heights read right to someone who has stood there, whether the wind sway distracts, and whether the frame budget holds with the full forest loaded.

Kittitas County, WA · 10 m · 1.45 M trees instanced within 4 km of the camera · UE 5.8.3, SM6 + Nanite · 2026-09-28

Flyover and wind

Bookmarks

Species silhouettes

One tree per species at its palette mid height (Douglas-fir 31.5 m, ponderosa 26.5 m, grand fir 28 m, sagebrush 1.4 m, bunchgrass 0.45 m) and a 1.8 m post, on the shore of Cooper Lake.

Results

  • Conformance exact. The renderer's C++ scatter reproduces Terrain's golden vectors, all 74,595 teanaway_dev trees and all 5,861,933 Three Queens trees, positions exact and attributes bit-equal.
  • Density follows the data. Trees per 10 m cell equal 4 × LANDFIRE canopy cover in every bin, from 40/ha at 10 % cover to 329/ha at 82 %. Species shares match the palette weights to 0.1 %.
  • Rendered canopy matches LANDFIRE cover. Crowns were drawn too wide and the forest read about 12 points denser than the data. Conifer crowns are now 0.23 × height (an 8 m crown on a 35 m fir) and rendered cover is within 0.4 points of LANDFIRE on average.
  • Budget met with full instancing.

Findings

  1. fixedThe renderer wasn't using Nanite. The project never set its shader model, so UE ran at SM5 (no Nanite, cascaded shadows), and the generated tree meshes had Nanite disabled. Both are fixed and the asset generator now fails if Nanite is off. HCP0 and HCP1 perf figures were SM5 numbers. Terrain captures didn't change except for sharper low-sun shadows.
  2. openHitches with the forest loaded. p95 is under budget, but about 13 frames in 300 spike to 35–160 ms while the render thread waits on the GPU. They don't happen without vegetation. This needs a profiler capture and is scheduled with the async tile loading before HCP6. Videos and stills are unaffected.
  3. expectedTrees are toys up close. Firs are stacked cones, ponderosa is a blob crown on a pole, and Douglas-fir and grand fir look alike. Crowns are solid, so stand interiors are dark. From 1 km up the forest reads right; below about 200 m it reads as a model.
  4. upstream U9Every tree gets its cell's canopy-top height. All three conifers average 33–34 m, there's no understory, and a re-clamp piles 270,000 ponderosa at exactly 45 m. This is Terrain's scatter rule, filed as a question.
  5. upstream U824,074 trees outside the AOI (0.4 %) have no ground under them. The renderer drops them.
  6. D11Trees stop 4 km from the camera. Past that, the terrain's canopy colouring carries the forest. The seam isn't visible at these poses; a mid-field tier belongs in the LOD plan.

Questions for you

  1. Density and heights: does the flyover read like this country? Should I take the understory question (U9) to Terrain, or are canopy-top heights fine at the product's viewing distances?
  2. Wind: the top of a 33 m tree moves about 0.4–0.85 m with gusts. Distracting, too little, or right?
  3. Trees up close: build better generated trees (branches and foliage cards, still from code) before HCP3, or park it until the camera work at HCP6 makes ground level matter?
  4. Budget: the forest uses 3.33 of 4 GB. Keep the 4 GB target and treat the 4 km tree radius as the knob?
